core.description: @tula/core, the TypeScript client. Its suite is apps/api/src/sdk-journeys.test.ts, which runs the journeys of apps/api/src/testing/sdk-journeys.ts for it.

expo.description: @tula/expo, the headless Expo SDK (packages/expo): the password, emailed and texted codes, passkeys through the platform’s sheet, provider sign-in through a system browser session, the second step and the session. Its suite is packages/expo/src/journeys.test.ts, which runs the same journeys for an ios client (an android one where the scenario is Android’s) with its refresh token in a secure store, a software authenticator behind the passkey sheet and the journey itself as the browser: under bun and not on a device.

swift.description: The Swift SDK (native/swift), an ios client with no screen: sign-up, sign-in with the password or an emailed code, a password reset and the session, with its refresh token behind a storage protocol. Its suite is native/swift/Tests/TulaAuthJourneyTests: XCTest methods that drive the client against the real API, which native/swift/fixture/server.ts serves in memory on a loopback port, on a macOS host and not on a device or in a simulator. native/swift/fixture/journeys.ts reads the journeys those tests declare and holds them to this list.

kotlin.description: The Kotlin SDK (native/android). No suite yet.

concurrent_refresh.description: Calls that need a token at the same moment, with the access token expired, share one refresh request and one result.

refresh_without_answer.description: A refresh that gets no answer (a timeout, a lost response) is repeated once, at once, with the same refresh token; an HTTP answer of any status is never repeated.

unknown_step_not_supported.description: A flow step the client does not know is shown as "not supported": it is handed to the application unchanged, never guessed at, never an error, and it signs nobody in.

session_kept_through_failed_refresh_offl.description: A refresh that cannot be made while the device is offline fails without ending the session: the client stays signed in, keeps its refresh token and refreshes when the network is back.
